Provide Cover: Identify your lead starfighter (Proton Torpedoes* required) and wingmen (if any). Turbolaser Batteries and TIEs with weapons may now target your starfighters (wingmen first, then lead if no wingmen remaining). Hit starfighters are immediately lost. It's Away!: Draw two destiny. '''PC Errata 2''' — [[Attack Run (PC Errata 2)]] (2_42) |label_versions=Versions |printed_title=＊アタック・ラン |printed_game_text=「デス・スター：トレンチ」に配備する。自分の移動フェイズに、以下の方法でアタック・ランを試みられる： トレンチへの突入：自分の宇宙戦闘機を最大で3機まで「トレンチ」に移動させる（フォースは不要）。ダークサイドは即座に3機までのタイを追跡に向かわせられる（フォースは不要）。 編隊を組む：宇宙戦闘機のうち1機を先頭機（「プロトン魚雷」*が必要）に指定し、残りがいるなら編隊僚機とする。「ターボレーザー砲塔」および兵器を配備しているタイは、この時点で反乱軍（ライトサイド）の宇宙戦闘機に向けて武器の使用を行う（最初は編隊僚機を狙い、それが全滅してから先頭機を攻撃する）。命中した宇宙戦闘機は即座にロストする。 発射したぞ！：運命数を2つ引く。 逃げろ、引き上げだ：宇宙戦闘機はすべて「デス・スター」星系カード上に移動する（フォースは不要）。 もし、（運命数の合計＋X＋Y－Z）＞15なら、デス・スターは“壊滅”する。 X＝先頭機パイロットの能力値。ただし「照準コンピュータ」が配備されている場合には3。 Y＝反乱軍の基地（ヤヴィン4またはホス）のうち最大のものにある位置カードの合計数。 Z＝その位置にいるタイのパイロットのうち最も能力値の高いものの値。 *アタック・ラン中には「オーバーロード」の影響を受けない。[[:File:Japanese-ANH-Attack-Run-SWCA-67653.jpg|Original Japanese printed face]]. |translation='''Title:''' Attack Run. '''Card text:''' Deploy on Death Star: Trench. During your move phase, you may attempt an Attack Run as follows: Enter the trench: Move up to 3 of your starfighters to the Trench (no Force). The Dark Side may immediately send up to 3 TIEs in pursuit (no Force). Form a squadron: Designate 1 starfighter as the lead (Proton Torpedoes* required); remaining starfighters, if any, are wingmen. Turbolaser Batteries and TIEs with weapons now fire at Rebel (Light Side) starfighters (wingmen first, then the lead after those are wiped out). Hit starfighters are immediately lost. Card Size | 63x88mm |} '''Reflections: A Collector's Bounty''' (sold as '''Reflections''') is the 23rd Star Wars CCG product, published by Decipher in January 2000. It is 114 foil cards (57 per side): 87 very rare foils, 25 super rare foils, and 2 ultra rare foils ([[Darth Vader]] and [[Luke Skywalker]]). Displays shipped with oversized, non-playable objective box toppers. Packs are 18 cards, MSRP $4.95, 30 packs per box. Each pack has '''one foil''' from the list below plus random reprints from earlier expansions. Those reprints are not listed here. A foil of a title not on this list is not a Reflections pack foil. It may be a later [[Promotional Foils|promotional foil]], a Japanese foil, or a counterfeit.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]. Title: R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo) Lore:
A small-bodied droid brimming with energy, loyal to his master and brave. A Rebel spy who is strong in adversity. Though 3PO derided him as a “cold-hearted philosopher,” his personality is rather the opposite. He is somewhat restless and sometimes acts unexpectedly.
Card text:
Adds +2 to the power, maneuver and hyperspeed of the starfighter he is aboard (+3 if Red 5). When he is at a place with an access link and the opponent draws destiny, activate 1 Force if it is 1–3. If it is 4–6, draw the top card of the Reserve Deck and add it to your hand.
=== Comparison with the English printing === The Japanese lore says that 3PO derided R2-D2 as a “cold-hearted philosopher”; the English face instead calls R2-D2 the “Incorrigible counterpart of a mindless philosopher.” The Japanese game text uses アクセス・リンク (access link) for the English Scomp link and states the two results directly, without words corresponding to the English “you may.” It expressly adds the drawn Reserve Deck card to the hand. The printed numerical statistics match the inspected English face. Neither inspected face prints a Nav Computer symbol; a later rule-derived capability must not be presented as a printed icon.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. The comparison uses the [[:File:ANH-L-r2d2.gif|original English card face]]. |see_also=* [[R2-D2 (Artoo-Detoo)|English counterpart]] * [[A New Hope (Japanese)#Card list|Japanese A New Hope card list]] * [[Translations of SWCCG#Japanese|Japanese printings]] |see_also_heading=See also |has_refs=1 |extra_sections=

Statistics

The printed values and symbols are shown above. The face prints one Droid symbol and the subtype 操縦ドロイド (astromech droid). It has no printed ability number and no printed Nav Computer, Pilot or Warrior symbol. Its lore identifies a Rebel spy.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 42 (Japanese card face), pp. 101–102 (checklist). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. Base landspeed is 1 under the character movement rule; this is a rule-derived value, not a printed statistic.[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0#Landspeed|Rulebook 2.0, Landspeed]]: “Characters have landspeed of 1.” The 1998 Glossary states that astromech droids provide nav computers. This is a rule-derived capability, separate from the absence of a printed Nav Computer symbol on this face.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], pp. 15 and 94, “astromech” and “nav computer icon”. The same Glossary gives droids no ability and gives droids without armor a defense value of zero.[[:File:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary (1998)]], p. 52, “droid”. |set_icon=[[File:Icon-set-A-New-Hope.png|20px|link=A New Hope Limited]] [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] }}

'''Virtual Modern Errata''' — [[Greedo (V) (Errata)]] (204_42) — current |sources=* Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080512224452/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html Greedo], [[Decipher]] (archived 12 May 2008). * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landyhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. '''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. |pulled_by=* [[Blizzard 4]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=General%20Veers Scomp: General Veers]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (General Veers; November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. |pulled_by=* [[Blizzard 4]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=General%20Veers Scomp: General Veers]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[General Veers (Reflections Foil)|General Veers (foil)]] |sources=* [[General Veers]] black-border printed face (3_87) * White-border product [[Revised Hoth]] * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4 [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. The shield generators will be down in moments, you may start your landing. * [[Imperial Command]] * general * leader * [[General Veers]] }}

'''Decipher (Reflections foil)''' — [[Greedo (Reflections Foil)|Greedo (foil)]] |sources=* [[Greedo]] black-border printed face (2_89) * White-border product [[Revised A New Hope]] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landy [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit value and special ability to "threaten" smugglers aren't great, but when combined with certain cards it can really be helpful. * [[Greeata]] * bounty hunter * Rodian }}

 == Editing the family navigator == This shared navigator appears in the Versions infobox of each article in the Premiere [[Darth Vader]] family. To update membership, use the '''Edit versions''' link on a member article or edit this template's source. Each publication entry uses [[Template:Card version link]] with its canonical article title and concise visible label. Use Show changes before saving, then check both the new article and existing family members. The current article highlights automatically. Add a verified publication here once and include {{Card versions/Darth Vader (Premiere)}} in its card template's versions field. Keep its existing images, text and identity. Era and set headings are linked, bold and underlined; publication entries use normal links. The PC errata of the Decipher card has its own explicitly labeled group, rather than assigning a later PC rewrite to the Decipher publishing era. This reversible Dark Side pilot covers the eleven existing family articles identified for the second test. The English Reflections foil is included with its independently verified physical foil face and publication identity. Other Vader personas, including [[Darth Vader, Dark Lord Of The Sith]] and [[Darth Vader With Lightsaber]], belong to their own card families.

Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Presence Of The Force (Errata)]] (1_227) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Presence Of The Force], [[Decipher]] (archived 4 August 2002). * Printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/images/presenceoftheforce.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Justin Pakeshttps://web.archive.org/web/20001010191601/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Imagine my dismay as I browsed the voluminous libraries of Deciphers card lists to discover that one of my favourite (proper English spelling there... :) cards was sans card extra. The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! Card Combos: [[Revolution]] + any Hut for a significant Force drain bonus. [[Revolution]] versus the [[Tatooine: Jundland Wastes]] + Expand the Empire card combo: Make the Dark Side regret using this popular Force drain strategy. [[Revolution]] is one of the few cards that can make a Dark Side Effect work for the Light Side. |combos=* [[Revolution]] + any Hut Significant Force drain bonus.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Revolution Scomp: Revolution]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec).
